hard_constraints: Ben is POV for this scene; Talon and Luke (by holo) are present.
Luke is a senior Master, not Grand Master; never reference 'As Grand Master' for himself.
Mortis is never named on-page; Luke's post-Crucible state is implication only (quieter, eyes further away, longer pauses).
The Skywalker apartment is the last Skywalker presence on Coruscant; the Jedi Order has no institutional foothold here.
The Foundation's public charitable work is real and genuine; Ben cannot morally flatten it.
Aelia is pressured toward stepping down to preserve the Foundation's mission; she is not arrested or criminally liable.
Korda is the dead public fall guy; the public story frames him as the rogue center.
The cover story is professionally constructed and emotionally true to ordinary viewers; it cannot be countered with the evidence Ben no longer has.
Ben, Talon, and Luke all see the cover is too neat and built in advance.
The only counter is showing up on Iresh before the operation completes.
Use Star Wars vocabulary: datapads not tablets, transparisteel not glass, durasteel not steel, turbolifts not elevators, comlinks not radios, blasters not guns, HoloNet not internet.
No ABY/BBY dating in narration or dialogue; characters reference events directly.
No real-world pop culture references, no film/book references, no Wookieepedia-style taxonomy.
No paragraph contains more than one invented bureaucratic/technical term; every technical phrase translates to immediate human stakes within two sentences.
Ben's interiority budget: max 150 words, max 2 paragraphs.
canon_risks: Risk of making Luke too conveniently fooled or absent; he is emotionally intelligent and sees the structural tell independently.
Risk of making the Foundation's public work seem hollow or performative; it is genuinely helpful to grieving families, which is why the cover story is effective.
Risk of making Aelia seem purely villainous; she is pressured to step down to protect the real charity, and her warmth is not an act.
Risk of over-explaining the post-Crucible texture; one quiet line of Luke's manner is sufficient.
Risk of using 'system' as default GAG metaphor; prefer logistics network, shipment trail, records chain, transfer chain, or operation.
Risk of making the cover story seem sloppy; it is professionally constructed and built in advance.
legends_continuity_notes: The Second Galactic Civil War (40-41 ABY) and the Yuuzhan Vong War (25-29 ABY) are the wars whose dead are named on the Foundation's scholarship walls.
The Foundation's scholarship walls include engraved names from Fondor, Kuat, and the refugee fleets.
The Jedi Order relocated to Shedu Maad in 44 ABY after the Senate voted to remove them from Coruscant following the Lost Tribe crisis.
Luke's post-Crucible state is from the 2013 novel Crucible by Troy Denning; Mortis is never named on-page.
The Skywalker apartment is the last Skywalker presence on Coruscant; the Coruscant Jedi Temple is no longer Order property.
The Galactic Alliance is under Chief of State Wynn Dorvan; the Dorvan administration has restored procedure, not trust.
possible_disney_bleed: Avoid 'World Between Worlds' (Disney Canon Force concept).
Avoid 'Inquisitorius' as a post-Imperial organization (Disney Canon structure).
Avoid 'kyber crystal bleeding' mechanic (Disney Canon lore).
Avoid 'The Way' as Mandalorian creed (Disney Canon).
Avoid 'Ben Solo' (Disney Canon character); 'Ben' is unambiguously Ben Skywalker.
required_context_for_drafter: The public story frames Korda as the rogue security director who hired illegal contractors; no Foundation culpability.
Aelia is pressured to step down to protect the Foundation's charitable mission; the warmth shown her is genuine.
The cover story is built in advance, not improvised; Tess prepared this narrative.
Ben, Talon, and Luke all see the structural tell: the story resolves too cleanly and too quickly for an organization that size.
The only evidence that can override the narrative is stopping the Iresh operation in real time.
The apartment's daytime light is cold-gray and dry; Talon has claimed the chair facing the door.
The news B-roll cuts to the scholarship walls Ben walked past in Ch 17; the real grief is being used as backdrop.
Ben's POV arc phase is 'moment_of_truth' (Midpoint pivot); he has already decided to go to Iresh, and this scene confirms there is no institutional alternative.
Luke's holo call is the third of three Book 1 conversations (Ch 3, Ch 16, Ch 20); this is the PP2 brief call from the apartment.
The scene closes the analytical phase; Ben and Talon continue preparing for Iresh.
allowed_au_divergences: The Shedu Maad Memorial Foundation (public charity) and the Vigil (hidden inner ring) are NEW post-war Coruscant-political institutions.
Greyline Strategic Services is a NEW organization.
Aevyn Soris is a NEW character (Jacen's side-project Force student).
The unfinished holocron and its contents (Recognition and Holding) are NEW artifacts.
The duplicated wartime manifest is a NEW artifact.
Iresh and the Glasswell are NEW locations.
The One Sith remain in pre-emergence; Legacy comics future is excised.
open_questions: None identified for this scene; all elements are covered by the supplied planning artifacts.
